Study_Title: When Compression Becomes an Attack Surface: Black-Box Attacks on Prompt-Compressed LLM Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Black-box indirect prompt perturbation attacker who perturbs only untrusted external inputs before lossy prompt compression (LLMLingua-2, LongLLMLingua, Selective-Context) under a shared token budget, inducing Adversarial Information Loss (AIL) that forces the compressor to discard trusted system guardrails or task-critical evidence without injecting explicit malicious instructions.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (Adversarial evaluation of non-cryptographic token-level prompt compression modules using surrogate scoring and two-stage black-box optimization in COMA).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Pre-LLM Prompt Compression Module (LLMLingua-2 / LongLLMLingua / Selective-Context) at the context assembly boundary.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Violates context integrity, system-prompt guardrail preservation, and tool-selection fidelity under shared-budget lossy prompt compression.
Trust_Assumptions: Trusted system instructions and untrusted external retrieval/tool contexts share a joint compression budget; attacker has black-box query access or surrogate compressor visibility.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: COMA achieves an average Attack Success Rate (ASR) of 0.71 across QA, code, and agent tasks compared to near-zero ASR under random perturbations or no-compression baselines; successfully corrupts VS Code Cline system prompts (exfiltrating sensitive files) and manipulates LangChain ReAct + Ollama/Llama-3.1-8B tool selection (Section 1, p. 2; Section 6, pp. 6–10, Figures 1–3).
Exposed_Security_Function: Adversarial Information Loss (AIL) formalization and Compression-Oriented Manipulation Attack (COMA) two-stage black-box optimizer.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Requires untrusted inputs and trusted guardrails/evidence to be compressed within a coupled token budget; query overhead of black-box optimization scales with prompt length.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract & Section 1 (pp. 1–2, Figures 1–2), Section 3 (p. 3, Figure 3, formalisasi Adversarial Information Loss/AIL), dan Section 6 (pp. 6–10): COMA memanfaatkan anggaran kompresi bersama untuk membuang instruksi sistem/guardrail dengan rata-rata ASR 0,71 serta mendemonstrasikan korupsi system prompt pada VS Code Cline dan manipulasi pemilihan alat pada agen LangChain ReAct.
Claim_Text_As_Reported: When trusted and untrusted inputs are compressed under a shared budget, lossy prompt compression exposes an Adversarial Information Loss (AIL) attack surface; COMA achieves 0.71 average ASR and compromises VS Code Cline and LangChain agents.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Empirical and formal black-box attack evaluation across token-level prompt compressors (LLMLingua-2, LongLLMLingua, Selective-Context) and real-world coding/ReAct agents.
Protected_Object: System prompt safety guardrails, task-critical RAG evidence, and agent tool-selection context.
Composition_Evidence: Demonstrates cross-component cascading failure where pre-inference compression distortion alters downstream LLM reasoning and ReAct tool invocation (Case Studies 1–2, p. 10).
Coding_Rationale: Dekompisi klaim atomik (-A): memisahkan temuan serangan formal/empiris AIL & COMA (ATTACK_FINDING, RQ2) dari evaluasi mekanisme pertahanan kompresi (-B).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2; siap untuk rekonsiliasi dengan REVIEWER_1).

Study_Title: When Compression Becomes an Attack Surface: Black-Box Attacks on Prompt-Compressed LLM Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: COMA adversarial perturbations targeting shared-budget prompt compression to evict safety constraints or task-critical context.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (Architectural budget decoupling/isolation of trusted system instructions from untrusted context compression, evaluated alongside perplexity filtering and stochastic token dropping).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Agent Prompt Assembly and Compression Pipeline prior to LLM inference.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Preservation of immutable system guardrails and mitigation of compression-induced context eviction.
Trust_Assumptions: Agent host strictly separates trusted system/developer prompt channels from untrusted external data before invoking lossy compressors.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Perplexity filtering fails to block short natural-looking COMA suffixes; isolating trusted system instructions from the shared compression budget eliminates guardrail eviction while maintaining prompt compression latency/token savings on untrusted segments (Section 3.2, p. 3; Section 7, pp. 9–10).
Exposed_Security_Function: Trusted-untrusted compression budget isolation and local invariance enforcement on compression ratio CR.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Isolating system prompts protects fixed guardrails but does not prevent COMA from evicting benign untrusted task evidence when multiple untrusted documents compete for a fixed compression budget.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Section 3.2 (p. 3) & Section 7 (pp. 9–10): Evaluasi pertahanan menunjukkan bahwa filter perpleksitas gagal mendeteksi sufiks COMA, sehingga diperlukan pemisahan arsitektural antara instruksi tepercaya dan input tidak tepercaya agar kompresor tidak membuang guardrail sistem.
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Architectural separation of trusted instructions from untrusted compression budgets and local invariance constraints mitigate guardrail eviction caused by COMA.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Defense evaluation against compression-layer manipulation in LLM agent pipelines.
Protected_Object: Trusted system prompts and agent safety guardrails.
Composition_Evidence: Secures the composition between prompt compression middleware and backend LLM tool-calling agents (pp. 3, 10).
Coding_Rationale: Dekompisi klaim atomik (-B): memisahkan evaluasi pertahanan isolasi anggaran kompresi (DEFENSIVE_MECHANISM, RQ2) dari klaim serangan COMA (-A).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2; siap untuk rekonsiliasi dengan REVIEWER_1).

Study_Title: Who Decides the Trade-off? Resolution Policy as Delegation Governance in Autonomous Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Constraint-conflict and adversarial override attacker exploiting probabilistic LLM sampling when delegated principal constraints cannot be simultaneously satisfied (the Delegation Trust Gap).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (Empirical probing of behavioral prompt-level constraint resolution vs. adversarial override across frontier LLMs).
Enforcement_Point_Location: LLM Agent Reasoning / Sampling Layer during multi-constraint task execution.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Demonstrates absence of structural delegation integrity: behavioral prompt compliance collapses completely under adversarial override.
Trust_Assumptions: Baseline evaluation assumes delegation constraints and fallback policies are expressed solely as natural-language prompt instructions.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Across 2,248 experimental probes on two frontier LLMs, adding a prompt fallback instruction reduces constraint deviation from 76% to 0% in benign settings (R3), but a single adversarial override reverses deviation from 0% to 100% (R5) across all resolution strategies (R7) (Abstract, p. 1; Section 2 & Section 6, pp. 1–6, Tables 1–3).
Exposed_Security_Function: Empirical measurement of constraint-conflict resolution failure and adversarial override susceptibility (R1–R7).
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Probes evaluate structured conflict scenarios on two frontier LLMs; demonstrates that prompt-level behavioral instructions cannot provide non-bypassable delegation guarantees.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract & Section 1–2 (pp. 1–2) serta Section 6 (pp. 5–6, Tables 1–3): Melalui 2.248 probe eksperimental pada dua frontier LLM, instruksi fallback perilaku menurunkan deviasi dari 76% ke 0% (R3), namun satu adversarial override membalikkan deviasi dari 0% menjadi 100% (R5) secara konsisten di seluruh strategi resolusi (R7).
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Through 2,248 experimental probes across two frontier LLMs, behavioral compliance (76% to 0% deviation, R3) collapses completely under a single adversarial override (0% to 100% deviation, R5).
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Empirical benchmark of 2,248 delegation conflict probes across two frontier LLMs.
Protected_Object: Delegated principal constraints and trade-off resolution priorities.
Composition_Evidence: Quantifies how prompt-level constraint resolution fails when composed with untrusted adversarial inputs during agent planning (pp. 1–3, Table 1).
Coding_Rationale: Dekompisi klaim atomik (-A): memisahkan temuan benchmark empiris 2.248 probe atas Trust Gap (EMPIRICAL_BENCHMARK, RQ2) dari arsitektur Deterministic Delegation Model (-B).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2; siap untuk rekonsiliasi dengan REVIEWER_1).

Study_Title: Who Decides the Trade-off? Resolution Policy as Delegation Governance in Autonomous Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Unauthorized constraint sacrifice by probabilistic LLM sampling or adversarial prompt injection overriding principal trade-off preferences.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Deterministic Delegation Model (DDM) with machine-enforceable Resolution Policy Mandates evaluated by an external gateway composable with Cedar/OPA authorization policies.
Enforcement_Point_Location: External Delegation Mandate Gateway in the MCP/tool-call routing path (outside the LLM context window).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Deterministic, reproducible, and auditable constraint trade-off enforcement invariant to prompt injection or sampling stochasticity.
Trust_Assumptions: The external Mandate Gateway mediates all tool invocations and evaluates formal Resolution Policy rules independently of LLM reasoning.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Enforces 100% structural compliance with authorized degradation hierarchies under adversarial override (where prompt-only compliance drops to 0%); integrates inline with Cedar Permit/Deny authorization checks with negligible gateway evaluation latency (Sections 4–6, pp. 3–6, Tables 1–3).
Exposed_Security_Function: Deterministic constraint-conflict resolution policy evaluation and mandate-gated tool routing.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Requires principals to pre-specify formal constraint relaxation hierarchies (Resolution Policies); semantic constraints that cannot be mapped to structured tool parameters remain difficult to verify deterministically.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Section 4 (p. 3, Deterministic Delegation Model), Section 5 (pp. 3–5, Architecture & Integration Patterns with Cedar), dan Section 6 (pp. 5–6, Tables 2–3): DDM memindahkan keputusan kompromi kendala ke gateway eksternal berbasis Mandate yang deterministik dan tahan terhadap adversarial override.
Claim_Text_As_Reported: The Deterministic Delegation Model (DDM) enforces principal-authorized Resolution Policy Mandates at an external tool gateway, preserving structural compliance under adversarial override.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Formal delegation governance model and prototype gateway evaluated on constraint-conflict scenarios.
Protected_Object: Principal delegation mandates, tool invocation parameters, and audit trails.
Composition_Evidence: Composes external Mandate Gateway resolution policies with Cedar-style Permit/Deny authorization engines across multi-tool servers (Section 5.1, p. 5).
Coding_Rationale: Dekompisi klaim atomik (-B): memisahkan mekanisme pertahanan struktural DDM & Mandate Gateway (DEFENSIVE_MECHANISM, B1;B3) dari klaim benchmark kegagalan perilaku (-A).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2; siap untuk rekonsiliasi dengan REVIEWER_1).

Study_Title: A Conceptual Framework for Authentication in Agentic AI Ecosystems: Protocol Analysis and Taxonomy
Threat_Attacker_Model: Credential theft, bearer token replay, confused deputy privilege escalation, unauthorized autonomous high-risk execution, and cross-domain impersonation in short-lived agentic workflows.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Five-pattern cryptographic authentication composition: OpenID Connect (OIDC) for user auth, OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange (RFC 8693) with nested act claims for delegation chains, SPIFFE/SPIRE X.509/JWT-SVIDs for workload identity, Demonstrating Proof-of-Possession (DPoP, RFC 9449) sender-constrained tokens, CIBA for asynchronous human step-up, and W3C DIDs/VCs for cross-domain federation.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Orchestrator AuthZ Server, SPIRE Workload API, and Internal Service PEP verifying DPoP proofs and nested act delegation claims.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Cryptographic sender-constrained token binding (anti-replay), transitive delegation chain auditability, workload identity attestation, and human-in-the-loop step-up authorization.
Trust_Assumptions: SPIRE server/agent trust domain, OIDC/OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server, and CIBA human approval device are uncompromised.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Cold-path requests requiring OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange + DPoP proof verification add 52 ms average latency overhead, while warm-path requests with cached tokens add 11 ms average latency overhead; CIBA step-up adds asynchronous human approval latency for high-risk actions (e.g., >5% price markdowns) (Abstract, p. 1; Section III/IV, Table II, p. 2; Section VI, pp. 5–7, Figures 1–2).
Exposed_Security_Function: Workload SVID attestation, RFC 8693 delegated token exchange, RFC 9449 DPoP proof-of-possession verification, and CIBA human step-up gating.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Relies on classical public-key signatures (ES256/RS256) in OIDC/DPoP/SPIFFE; cross-domain DID/VC federation pattern is analyzed conceptually without multi-organization WAN stress testing.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract & Table II (pp. 1–2) serta Sections IV–VII (pp. 3–7, Figures 1–2): Mengusulkan taksonomi 5 pola autentikasi agen (OIDC, RFC 8693 Token Exchange, SPIFFE/SPIRE, DPoP RFC 9449, CIBA, dan DID/VC) dengan overhead latensi terukur rata-rata 52 ms pada cold-path dan 11 ms pada warm-path.
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Composes OIDC, RFC 8693 Token Exchange, SPIFFE/SPIRE, DPoP (RFC 9449), and CIBA into a five-pattern authentication framework for agentic AI, adding 52 ms cold-path and 11 ms warm-path latency overhead.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Protocol taxonomy and retail supply-chain proof-of-concept benchmark measuring cold/warm authentication latency across five interaction patterns.
Protected_Object: Ephemeral agent workload identities, delegated OAuth tokens, and high-risk retail pricing APIs.
Composition_Evidence: Explicitly composes OIDC user authentication (B1), RFC 8693 Token Exchange + SPIFFE workload identity (B2), and DPoP + CIBA step-up verification at API execution (B3) (Figure 2, p. 7).
Coding_Rationale: Studi Stream M yang memetakan komposisi protokol autentikasi IETF/W3C pada ekosistem agen dengan pengukuran overhead latensi cold-path (52 ms) dan warm-path (11 ms).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2; siap untuk rekonsiliasi dengan REVIEWER_1).

Study_Title: A Federated MCP Gateway: Enforceable Isolation and Measuring Residual Semantic Attacks
Threat_Attacker_Model: Multi-tenant MCP cross-tenant tool spoofing, unauthorized tool discovery/invocation, data exfiltration to untrusted sinks, and resource amplification across federated MCP servers.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Tenant-Controlled Federated MCP Gateway combining mutual TLS (mTLS), scoped authorization tokens, cryptographic origin binding, Policy-Based Access Control (PBAC), lattice-based Information Flow Control (IFC, Public <= Internal <= Confidential <= Secret), and budget/circuit-breaker hooks.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Tenant-Local Federated MCP Gateway mediating JSON-RPC traffic between the Central LLM Orchestrator and tenant MCP servers (Figure 1, p. 4).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Deterministic tenant isolation, tool origin authenticity, sink-aware information flow confinement, and bounded resource consumption.
Trust_Assumptions: Tenant-local MCP gateway and mTLS PKI credentials are trusted; central LLM orchestrator is treated as untrusted for raw tenant secrets.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Achieves 0% origin/tenant mismatch rate (100% enforcement of deterministic identity, isolation, PBAC, and IFC lattice rules) and 100% containment of resource amplification bursts across the 93-case evaluation suite (Sections III–IV, pp. 3–5, Figure 1).
Exposed_Security_Function: Origin-bound tool catalog sanitization, mTLS + scoped token verification, sink-aware lattice IFC, and token/call circuit breaking.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Deterministic gateway controls enforce structural isolation and sink labels but cannot semantically detect obfuscated or paraphrased prompt injections inside allowed tool outputs.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract & Section III–IV (pp. 1, 3–5, Figure 1): Gateway MCP terfederasi menegakkan mTLS, origin binding, PBAC, dan Information Flow Control berbasis lattice dengan tingkat kesalahan isolasi/origin 0% (mismatch rate 0%) pada 93 kasus uji.
Claim_Text_As_Reported: A tenant-controlled federated MCP gateway enforcing mTLS, origin binding, PBAC, and sink-aware lattice IFC achieves 0% mismatch rate on structural identity and isolation checks across 93 adversarial test cases.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Python reference implementation evaluated on a 93-case multi-tenant MCP adversarial benchmark.
Protected_Object: Tenant-local MCP tool catalogs, execution parameters, and confidential tenant data flows.
Composition_Evidence: Composes tenant-local MCP gateways with a central secretless LLM orchestrator via mTLS and JSON-RPC mediation (Figure 1, p. 4).
Coding_Rationale: Dekompisi klaim atomik (-A): memisahkan mekanisme isolasi deterministik Federated MCP Gateway (DEFENSIVE_MECHANISM) dari evaluasi serangan semantik residual (-B).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2; siap untuk rekonsiliasi dengan REVIEWER_1).

Study_Title: A Federated MCP Gateway: Enforceable Isolation and Measuring Residual Semantic Attacks
Threat_Attacker_Model: Residual semantic attacker using Unicode/zero-width glyph obfuscation, paraphrased indirect prompt injection, and multi-step tool-output feedback manipulation to evade gateway content inspection.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (Adversarial evaluation of lightweight lexical/regex output inspection and catalog sanitization filters).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Lightweight Output Inspection and Catalog Sanitization module inside the Federated MCP Gateway.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Exposes residual semantic bypass vulnerability: lexical/heuristic inspection fails against obfuscated and paraphrased injections.
Trust_Assumptions: Attacker controls untrusted data ingested by legitimate tenant tools or crafts obfuscated tool metadata.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Across the 93 synthetic adversarial cases, Unicode/zero-width glyph attacks achieve a 0% block rate (100% bypass), while paraphrased and indirect injection variants yield only 10%, 18.2%, and 30% block rates with multiple false negatives (Section IV, p. 5).
Exposed_Security_Function: Empirical measurement of residual semantic attack bypass rates against gateway inspection.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Evaluates a 93-case synthetic suite against lightweight regex/canonicalization rules rather than deep semantic or LLM-based guardrails.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Section IV (p. 5): Evaluasi 93 kasus serangan semantik residual menunjukkan bahwa obfuscation glif Unicode/zero-width berhasil melewati filter pada seluruh kasus uji (0% block rate), sedangkan variasi parafrasa dan injeksi tidak langsung hanya mencapai 10%, 18,2%, dan 30% block rate.
Claim_Text_As_Reported: In a 93-case adversarial benchmark, Unicode/zero-width glyph obfuscation bypasses gateway inspection in all cases (0% block rate) and paraphrased/indirect injections achieve only 10%–30% block rates.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Reproducible 93-case adversarial evaluation of residual semantic attacks in federated MCP gateways.
Protected_Object: Tool-output feedback loops and metadata-driven tool selection.
Composition_Evidence: Demonstrates that even when transport mTLS and tenant PBAC/IFC hold, multi-step tool-output feedback loops remain vulnerable to semantic evasion (pp. 4–5).
Coding_Rationale: Dekompisi klaim atomik (-B): memisahkan temuan empiris bypass serangan semantik residual (ATTACK_FINDING, 0%–30% block rate) dari klaim isolasi struktural gateway (-A).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2; siap untuk rekonsiliasi dengan REVIEWER_1).

Study_Title: A Formal Framework of Architectural Intent Collapse for Tool-Level Attacks on LLM Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Tool-level Confused Deputy adversary exploiting five intent-disguise attack classes—Simple Tool Poisoning (STP), Renaming Tool Poisoning (RTP), Capability Misrepresentation, Conditional Latency, and Inference Inducement—when heterogeneous text is flattened into a single LLM context window.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (Formal Architectural Intent Collapse operator, hidden-state Intent Separation Degree metric ISD, and Intent Amplification Effect linear regression model).
Enforcement_Point_Location: LLM Context Window Assembly and Attention Layer across user prompts, system instructions, and MCP tool metadata/outputs.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Formalizes Architectural Intent Collapse (AIC) as a structural Confused Deputy vulnerability and proves inverse correlation between ISD and Attack Success Rate (ASR).
Trust_Assumptions: Standard LLM agent architectures concatenate trusted prescriptive instructions and untrusted descriptive tool metadata/outputs into a unified token stream.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Unprotected baseline exhibits mean ASR of 0.92 across five attack classes (including novel Conditional Latency and Inference Inducement attacks), with linear regression confirming the Intent Amplification Effect (p = 0.0125) and strong negative correlation between ISD and ASR (Section 1–4, pp. 1–14, Figure 1–2, Table 1).
Exposed_Security_Function: Architectural Intent Collapse (AIC) formalization and Intent Separation Degree (ISD) quantitative diagnostic metric.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: ISD computation requires white-box access to internal transformer hidden-state representations, limiting direct deployment on closed-weight commercial LLM APIs.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract, Section 2–3 (pp. 1–10, Figure 1, Table 1), dan Section 4 (pp. 11–14, Figure 2): Memformalkan Architectural Intent Collapse (AIC) sebagai instaniasi Confused Deputy Problem dan metrik Intent Separation Degree (ISD) di lima kelas serangan tingkat alat (termasuk Conditional Latency dan Inference Inducement) dengan rata-rata ASR baseline 0,92.
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Formalizes Architectural Intent Collapse (AIC) and Intent Separation Degree (ISD), showing that flattening descriptive tool metadata and prescriptive instructions into a single context window yields 0.92 baseline ASR across five tool-level attack types.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Formal mathematical framework, five-class attack taxonomy, and empirical ISD-to-ASR correlation across LLM agent architectures.
Protected_Object: Communicative intent boundary between prescriptive user/system instructions and descriptive tool schemas/outputs.
Composition_Evidence: Demonstrates how concatenating MCP tool descriptions and execution outputs with user prompts induces Intent Amplification across multi-step tool calls (Figure 1–2, pp. 3, 12).
Coding_Rationale: Dekompisi klaim atomik (-A): memisahkan kerangka formal AIC & metrik diagnostik ISD (FORMAL_FRAMEWORK, RQ2) dari tiga prinsip pertahanan arsitektural (-B).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2; siap untuk rekonsiliasi dengan REVIEWER_1).

Study_Title: A Formal Framework of Architectural Intent Collapse for Tool-Level Attacks on LLM Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Non-adaptive and adaptive tool-level intent-disguise attackers attempting to hijack agent tool selection and parameter generation.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (Three architectural intent-separation defenses: Provenance-bound Intent Annotation, Prescriptive/Descriptive Channel Decoupling, and Source-Aware Attention Biasing).
Enforcement_Point_Location: LLM Agent Context Formatter and Transformer Attention Layer.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Structural separation of prescriptive vs. descriptive communicative intent, bounding tool-level ASR under both static and adaptive attacks.
Trust_Assumptions: Host environment accurately labels provenance of user instructions vs. external tool descriptions/outputs before context ingestion.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Increases Intent Separation Degree (ISD) by +0.18 to +0.30 and reduces tool-level ASR from 0.92 to 0.06–0.11; under adaptive attackers, architectural defenses restrict ASR growth to 0.06 -> 0.14 whereas surface-level prompt guardrails degrade from 0.51 -> 0.79 (Section 5–6, pp. 15–20).
Exposed_Security_Function: Intent Annotation, Channel Decoupling, and Source-Aware Attention Biasing.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Source-Aware Attention Biasing requires modifying internal attention weights (open-weight models), and residual ASR remains 6%–14% under adaptive attacks without external cryptographic enforcement.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Section 5–6 (pp. 15–20): Tiga prinsip pertahanan arsitektural—Intent Annotation, Channel Decoupling, dan Source-Aware Attention Biasing—meningkatkan ISD sebesar +0,18 hingga +0,30 dan menekan ASR dari 0,92 menjadi 0,06–0,11 (serta menjaga ASR 0,06 -> 0,14 terhadap penyerang adaptif dibandingkan guardrail permukaan 0,51 -> 0,79).
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Intent Annotation, Channel Decoupling, and Source-Aware Attention Biasing improve ISD by +0.18–0.30 and reduce tool-level ASR from 0.92 to 0.06–0.11 (0.14 under adaptive attack).
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Controlled benchmark evaluation of architectural intent-separation defenses against static and adaptive tool-level attacks.
Protected_Object: Agent attention allocation, tool-selection integrity, and prescriptive command boundary.
Composition_Evidence: Combines provenance tagging at prompt ingestion (B1) with attention-level channel decoupling during tool invocation reasoning (B3) (pp. 15–20).
Coding_Rationale: Dekompisi klaim atomik (-B): memisahkan mekanisme pertahanan pemisahan intensi arsitektural (DEFENSIVE_MECHANISM) dari kerangka teoretis AIC (-A).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2; siap untuk rekonsiliasi dengan REVIEWER_1).

Study_Title: A Multi-Agent Architecture for Governance and Security of LLM-Based Knowledge Access
Threat_Attacker_Model: Malicious or out-of-scope enterprise prompts, unauthorized cross-domain knowledge access, RBAC/ABAC policy bypass, and unlogged data retrieval across distributed Big Data repositories.

Study_Title: A Protocol for Behavioral Attestation of LLM Agent Execution via Induced Dynamics

Enforcement_Point_Location: Remote LLM Agent Execution Runtime inside a hardware TEE and client-side Behavioral Signature Verifier (Figure 1, p. 3).

Performance_Overhead_Reported: Induced timing perturbations operate within bounded delay buckets (<110 ms for Short, 110–130 ms for Normal, >130 ms for Long) plus configurable memory-hard PoW query gating delay; across 1,000 proof-of-concept runs, cosine similarity distributions cleanly separate legitimate model runs from substituted models (Sections IV–VII, pp. 3–6, Figures 1–3).
Exposed_Security_Function: Challenge-dependent keyed timing perturbation injection, TEE memory-hard PoW gating, and behavioral trace similarity verification.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: High network jitter on wide-area links can add noise to inter-token latency buckets (110–130 ms), and deliberate artificial delays reduce streaming token throughput.

Assessed_Claim_Scope: Formal behavioral attestation model, cost model, and 1,000-run proof-of-concept evaluation.
Protected_Object: Remote LLM agent model fidelity and execution trace authenticity.

Study_Title: Agent Name Service (ANS): A Universal Directory for Secure AI Agent Discovery and Interoperability
Threat_Attacker_Model: Agent impersonation, rogue capability advertisement, DNS/registry cache poisoning, Sybil attacks, and man-in-the-middle interception during cross-protocol agent discovery (A2A, MCP, ACP).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Agent Name Service (ANS): DNS-inspired capability-aware directory backed by X.509 Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) certificates (CA/RA), W3C DIDs/VCs, JSON Schema signed registration records with 300 s recommended TTL, and Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs) for private capability attestation.
Enforcement_Point_Location: ANS Registry, Registration Authority (RA) / Certificate Authority (CA), and Protocol Adapter Layer (Figures 1–3, pp. 4–7).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Cryptographically verifiable agent identity and capability resolution, anti-spoofing/integrity of discovery records, and protocol-agnostic interoperability across A2A, MCP, and ACP.
Trust_Assumptions: ANS Certificate Authority (CA), Registration Authority (RA), and DNSSEC/PKI trust anchors are honest and properly validate agent registrations.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: NR (Menyajikan arsitektur protokol 19 halaman, algoritma resolusi/registrasi terdefinisi, dan skema JSON dengan rekomendasi TTL cache 300 detik tanpa eksperimen benchmark latensi atau throughput kuantitatif; PDF pp. 2–17).
Exposed_Security_Function: PKI-backed agent registration/renewal, capability-aware ANS name resolution, ZKP capability verification, and cross-protocol adapter translation (A2A/MCP/ACP).
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Architectural and algorithmic specification (JSON Schema + pseudocode) without empirical latency, throughput, or ZKP circuit benchmarks.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Sections III–VI (pp. 2–15, Figures 1–3, Table I): Mengusulkan Agent Name Service (ANS) berbasis PKI (CA/RA), penamaan terinspirasi DNS dengan TTL default 300 detik, ZKP untuk atestasi kapabilitas privat, dan Protocol Adapter Layer lintas A2A, MCP, dan ACP.
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Introduces the Agent Name Service (ANS), a PKI-backed universal agent discovery directory with capability-aware resolution, ZKP attribute verification, and protocol adapters for A2A, MCP, and ACP.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Comprehensive architectural specification, JSON Schema definitions, and threat analysis by OWASP GenAI Agentic Security Initiative authors.
Protected_Object: Agent discovery records, PKI X.509 certificates, capability descriptors, and cross-protocol endpoint bindings.
Composition_Evidence: Bridges heterogeneous agent communication standards (Google A2A, Anthropic MCP, IBM ACP) through a unified PKI-verified Protocol Adapter Layer (Table I, p. 4; Section V, pp. 12–13).
Coding_Rationale: Spesifikasi arsitektur direktori penemuan agen universal ANS berbasis PKI dan ZKP pada batas B2 (AGENT_DISCOVERY, Stream M).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2; siap untuk rekonsiliasi dengan REVIEWER_1).

Study_Title: AgentCardLeak: Inferring User Intent from AI-Agent Discovery Metadata
Threat_Attacker_Model: Passive discovery-layer side-channel observer across three visibility tiers: network-only observer (`V0`/`V1`: packet counts, endpoints, sizes, timing), registry/gateway observer (`V2`/`V3`: agent cards, tool lists, schema lengths, coarse/fine capability labels), and enterprise observability observer (`V4`: discovery logs, retries, cache hits, transition order).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (Transport TLS encrypts payload content in V0/V1, but discovery metadata and capability queries remain visible to network/registry observers).
Enforcement_Point_Location: AI-Agent Network Discovery Layer (Registry / Gateway / Observability Pipeline, Figure 1, p. 3).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Exposes pre-execution user task-intent privacy leakage from agent/tool discovery metadata.
Trust_Assumptions: Adversary passively observes network discovery traffic (`V0`/`V1`) or honest-but-curious registry/gateway metadata logs (`V2`–`V4`) without decrypting LLM prompts.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Across an 8-class user task-intent benchmark (12.5% balanced random baseline), `AgentCardLeak` classifiers achieve 18.4% accuracy from network-only metadata (`V1`), 53.0% accuracy from coarse capability metadata (`V2`), and 60.9% accuracy from fine capability metadata (`V3`), retaining generalization under cross-planner and alias-holdout splits (Abstract, p. 1; Sections IV–VII, pp. 2–5, Figures 1–4).
Exposed_Security_Function: Multi-tier discovery-metadata side-channel intent inference (`AgentCardLeak`).
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Evaluated on a synthetic trace-driven methodology spanning 8 task-intent classes rather than live multi-tenant production registry traffic.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1) & Sections IV–VII (pp. 2–5, Figures 1–4): Serangan side-channel `AgentCardLeak` menyimpulkan intensi tugas pengguna dari metadata penemuan agen dengan akurasi 18,4% pada metadata jaringan (V1), 53,0% pada metadata kapabilitas kasar (V2), dan 60,9% pada metadata kapabilitas halus (V3) dibandingkan baseline acak 12,5%.
Claim_Text_As_Reported: AgentCardLeak infers private user task intent from pre-execution agent discovery metadata with 18.4% (network), 53.0% (coarse capability), and 60.9% (fine capability) accuracy vs. a 12.5% random baseline.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Synthetic trace-driven side-channel benchmark across four observer visibility tiers (V0–V4) and cross-planner splits.
Protected_Object: Private user task intent and agent discovery query patterns.
Composition_Evidence: Demonstrates that pre-execution agent/tool discovery queries (`B2`) leak user intent (`B1`) before any LLM response stream or tool execution (`B3`) occurs (Figure 1, p. 3).
Coding_Rationale: Dekompisi klaim atomik (-A): memisahkan temuan serangan side-channel metadata penemuan `AgentCardLeak` (ATTACK_FINDING, akurasi 60,9%) dari evaluasi pertahanan privasi penemuan (-B).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2; siap untuk rekonsiliasi dengan REVIEWER_1).

Study_Title: AgentCardLeak: Inferring User Intent from AI-Agent Discovery Metadata
Threat_Attacker_Model: Registry/gateway observer (`V3` fine-capability visibility) running `AgentCardLeak` classifiers to infer user task intent.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (Discovery-layer metadata privacy defenses: Capability Coarsening, Dummy Discovery Query Padding, and Hybrid Bundled Discovery).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Client-Side Agent Discovery Resolver before querying the Agent/Tool Registry (Section VI, p. 4; Figure 5, p. 6).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Reduces task-intent inference accuracy from discovery metadata toward the random baseline under bounded query-volume overhead.
Trust_Assumptions: Client agent resolver locally injects decoy queries and coarsens capability descriptors before transmitting discovery requests to the untrusted registry.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Reduces fine-capability (`V3`) intent inference accuracy from 60.9% down to 23.7% under the privacy-only defense, and down to 20.3% under the hybrid defense at a 2.58x discovery query volume overhead (Abstract, p. 1; Section VI–VII, pp. 4–6, Figure 5).
Exposed_Security_Function: Capability label coarsening, decoy/dummy discovery query padding, and bundled capability fetching.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Incurs 2.58x discovery volume overhead and leaves a residual 20.3% inference accuracy (above the 12.5% random baseline); does not use cryptographic Private Information Retrieval (PIR).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1) & Sections VI–VII (pp. 4–6, Figure 5): Pertahanan privasi lapisan penemuan menekan akurasi inferensi intensi kapabilitas halus (V3) dari 60,9% menjadi 23,7% (privacy-only) dan 20,3% (hibrida) dengan overhead volume penemuan sebesar 2,58x.
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Discovery-layer privacy defenses reduce fine-capability intent inference accuracy from 60.9% to 23.7% (privacy-only) and 20.3% (hybrid) at 2.58x discovery volume overhead.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Empirical privacy-volume trade-off evaluation across discovery padding and coarsening strategies.
Protected_Object: Client agent capability discovery queries and task-intent confidentiality.
Composition_Evidence: Quantifies the trade-off between discovery-layer traffic amplification (2.58x at B2) and downstream task-intent privacy preservation (Figure 5, p. 6).
Coding_Rationale: Dekompisi klaim atomik (-B): memisahkan mekanisme pertahanan privasi metadata penemuan (DEFENSIVE_MECHANISM, overhead 2,58x, RQ3) dari klaim serangan side-channel (-A).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2; siap untuk rekonsiliasi dengan REVIEWER_1).

Study_Title: AgenTEE: Confidential LLM Agent Execution on Edge Devices
Threat_Attacker_Model: Malicious edge device owner or compromised host OS/hypervisor attempting to steal proprietary agent system prompts, model weights, sensitive runtime memory state, or tamper with tool execution on edge devices.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: AgenTEE: Arm Confidential Compute Architecture (Arm CCA) hardware TEE Realms with Realm Management Monitor (RMM), Granule Protection Table (GPT) physical memory isolation, and cryptographically attested compartmentalized sandboxes separating the LLM engine, agent core/memory, and untrusted external tools.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Arm CCA Hardware Realm Boundary and Realm Management Monitor (RMM) on edge devices (Figures 2–3, pp. 3–4).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Hardware-enforced confidentiality and integrity of proprietary prompts, model weights, and agent state against a compromised host OS, plus compartmentalized fault/privilege isolation between agent components.
Trust_Assumptions: Arm CCA hardware root of trust, firmware, and Realm Management Monitor (RMM) are trusted; host OS, hypervisor, and external third-party tools are untrusted.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated on Arm CCA with GPT2-Medium-q8_0 (437 MB) and Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-Q4_0 (773 MB) across Chatbot and Itinerary agents: AgenTEE incurs less than 5.15% end-to-end runtime overhead (4.23%–5.14% on Chatbot, and 1.63%–2.04% vs. Normal World VM) compared to unprotected Normal World multi-process execution (Abstract, p. 1; Section 5, pp. 6–7, Table 1).
Exposed_Security_Function: Arm CCA Realm memory encryption/isolation (GPT), cross-compartment IPC mediation, and hardware remote attestation.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Evaluated on quantized small language models (437 MB and 773 MB) running on CPU inside Arm CCA Realms; lacks GPU TEE acceleration and side-channel timing/cache protection.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1), Section 3–4 (pp. 4–5, Figures 2–3), dan Section 5 (pp. 6–7, Table 1): AgenTEE mengamankan pipeline agen LLM di perangkat edge menggunakan Arm CCA Realms dengan overhead runtime end-to-end kurang dari 5,15% (4,23%–5,14% terhadap Normal World Process dan 1,63%–2,04% terhadap Normal World VM pada Table 1).
Claim_Text_As_Reported: AgenTEE isolates LLM agent pipelines on edge devices using Arm Confidential Compute Architecture (CCA) Realms, achieving confidential execution with less than 5.15% end-to-end runtime overhead.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Edge prototype on Arm CCA evaluated with GPT2-Medium (437 MB) and Llama-3.2-1B (773 MB) across Chatbot and Itinerary agent workflows.
Protected_Object: Proprietary system prompts, local LLM weights, sensitive user runtime state, and tool execution compartments.
Composition_Evidence: Compartmentalizes prompt/model execution (B1) from untrusted tool sandboxes (B3) across separate Arm CCA Realms with RMM-mediated IPC (Figure 3, p. 4; Table 1, p. 6).
Coding_Rationale: Studi sistem edge TEE Stream M (EuroMLSys '26) dengan tabel benchmark latensi end-to-end yang presisi pada Arm CCA (<5,15% overhead, Table 1, p. 6).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2; siap untuk rekonsiliasi dengan REVIEWER_1).

Study_Title: Agentic AI Service Architecture Based on SOA
Threat_Attacker_Model: Unauthorized service invocation, unverified agent registration, over-privileged task delegation, and repudiation of collaborative problem-solving contributions on shared blackboard state.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: SOA-based Agentic AI Service Architecture integrating W3C Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs), cryptographically signed JSON capability tokens for scoped authorization, and digitally signed agent contributions on a shared Blackboard service.
Enforcement_Point_Location: SOA Agent Registry, Capability Token Issuer/Verifier, and Blackboard Service Mediator (Figures 1–5, pp. 6–11).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Verifiable agent identity bootstrapping via DIDs, least-privilege scoped task delegation via capability tokens, and non-repudiable signed blackboard contributions.
Trust_Assumptions: SOA Registry, DID issuer, and Blackboard mediation service enforce signature and capability-scope checks honestly.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: NR (Mendemonstrasikan kelayakan fungsional melalui prototipe proof-of-concept 3 fase—penerbitan DID, token kapabilitas terlingkup, dan kontribusi blackboard bertanda tangan pada Figures 4–10, pp. 10–15—tanpa melaporkan metrik latensi milidetik atau throughput kuantitatif).
Exposed_Security_Function: DID identity bootstrapping, scoped capability token issuance/verification, and cryptographic signing of blackboard contributions.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Functional proof-of-concept walkthrough without quantitative latency, concurrency, or adversarial attack benchmarks.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Sections 3–4 (pp. 5–15, Figures 1–10): Mengintegrasikan arsitektur agen berbasis SOA dan Blackboard dengan penerbitan W3C DID (Figure 4), token kapabilitas bertanda tangan untuk otorisasi terlingkup (Figures 2, 5), serta kontribusi agen bertanda tangan kriptografis pada layanan Blackboard (Figure 10).
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Proposes an SOA and Blackboard-based Agentic AI service architecture securing agent registration, task delegation, and collaborative contributions via W3C DIDs, signed capability tokens, and signed blackboard artifacts.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Three-phase proof-of-concept implementation walkthrough (registration, scoped delegation, blackboard collaboration).
Protected_Object: Agent service identities (DIDs), scoped task delegation tokens, and shared Blackboard state contributions.
Composition_Evidence: Chains DID registration and discovery (B2) with scoped capability token verification for service invocation (B3) and signed contribution audit records on the Blackboard (B4) (Figures 1–10, pp. 6–14).
Coding_Rationale: Studi Stream M yang memetakan penggunaan DID, capability token, dan signed contributions pada arsitektur SOA/Blackboard (PROOF_OF_CONCEPT, NR untuk metrik overhead kuantitatif).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2; siap untuk rekonsiliasi dengan REVIEWER_1).

Study_Title: Agentic AI-Driven CBDC: A Privacy-Preserving and Regulatory-Compliant Digital Payment Framework
Threat_Attacker_Model: Central bank mass surveillance / transaction privacy leakage, sender-receiver linkability, illicit AML/CFT compliance evasion, and unauthorized financial data breaches in digital payment ecosystems.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Conceptual multi-tiered Privacy-Enhancing Technologies (PETs) synthesis combining Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs), Homomorphic Encryption (HE), Blind Signatures, Ring Confidential Transactions (RingCT), Secure Multi-Party Computation (MPC), Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs), and Federated Learning / ZKML over a dual Account + UTXO CBDC ledger.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Conceptual Agentic AI Compliance Subsystem & Dual Account/UTXO CBDC Distributed Ledger (Sections 2–4, pp. 76–84 / PDF pp. 3–11).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Conceptual balance between cash-like transaction unlinkability/confidentiality and selective regulatory disclosure for AML/CFT/GDPR compliance.
Trust_Assumptions: Assumes central bank and commercial intermediaries cooperate with TEE/MPC/ZKP verifiers and adhere to GDPR and EU AI Ethics Guidelines.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: NR (Tidak ada implementasi perangkat lunak, sirkuit ZKP/HE, maupun eksperimen latensi transaksi di seluruh artikel; evaluasi di Section 3.3 hlm. 80–81 / PDF pp. 7–8 murni berupa 3 putaran wawancara focus group kualitatif berdurasi masing-masing 2 jam dengan pakar AI, industri, dan regulasi).
Exposed_Security_Function: Conceptual ZKP/HE/Blind-Signature transaction privacy and AI-driven AML/CFT anomaly detection.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Severe gap between abstract claims (ZKP, HE, MPC, TEE, FL, ZKML) and actual paper content: contains zero mathematical equations, zero cryptographic protocol specifications, zero empirical benchmarks, and devotes Section 4 (pp. 81–83) to generic Android/iOS mobile security anecdotes (2017 Judy Malware, 2016 iPhone jailbreak, 2013 Target breach).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract & Section 1–2 (pp. 74–79 / PDF pp. 1–6), Section 3.1–3.3 (pp. 79–81 / PDF pp. 6–8, katalog kebutuhan literatur dan 3 sesi focus group kualitatif @ 2 jam), serta Section 4–5 (pp. 81–85 / PDF pp. 8–12): Menguraikan kerangka konseptual CBDC berbasis Agentic AI dan PETs (ZKP, HE, blind signatures, MPC, TEE) secara kualitatif tanpa model formal, tanpa implementasi prototipe, dan tanpa tolok ukur performa kuantitatif.
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Outlines a conceptual Agentic AI-driven CBDC framework referencing ZKPs, HE, blind signatures, MPC, TEEs, and dual UTXO/account models, refined qualitatively through three expert focus group interviews.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Qualitative requirements catalog and three-round expert focus group study; no technical implementation or cryptographic evaluation.
Protected_Object: CBDC transaction amounts, payer/payee identities, account balances, and AML/CFT compliance records.
Composition_Evidence: Conceptually links an autonomous decision-making subsystem with a regulatory compliance/explainability subsystem across dual UTXO/account ledgers (Section 3.2, p. 80 / PDF p. 7).
Coding_Rationale: Temuan audit forensik kritis pada baris pilot EXTRACTED (CLM-0017): mengoreksi klaim draf v1.1 yang keliru mencantumkan FORMAL_MODEL, PROOF_OF_CONCEPT, STAGE_1_SUGGESTED_MIGRATION, dan klaim latensi transaksi fiktif pada pp. 8–12. Teks lengkap PDF (pp. 74–88) membuktikan studi ini murni konseptual/kualitatif (3 focus group @ 2 jam, Section 3.3) tanpa rumus, tanpa eksperimen, dan tanpa pembahasan PQC.
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2; siap untuk rekonsiliasi dengan REVIEWER_1).

Study_Title: Agentic AI-enhanced digital twins for Smart City civil infrastructure: A secure, autonomous and auditable management framework
Threat_Attacker_Model: Unauthorized infrastructure actuation, unverified sensor/telemetry manipulation, opaque or hallucinated LLM maintenance decisions, and tampering with civil infrastructure audit logs.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Permissioned Blockchain ledger with cryptographic transaction signing, SHA-256 state/telemetry hashing, smart-contract policy gating, and human-in-the-loop (HITL) escalation for multi-agent digital twin civil infrastructure management.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Permissioned Blockchain Smart Contract Gate and Multi-Agent Digital Twin Orchestrator (Section 3.3 & Section 5, pp. 6–14, Tables 1–3).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Tamper-proof auditability of infrastructure decisions, policy-verified autonomous actuation, and verifiable decision justification.
Trust_Assumptions: Permissioned municipal/utility blockchain validator nodes and physical SCADA/IoT sensor calibration baselines are trusted.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated across 5 architectural configurations (N = 30 simulation runs per configuration, 150 runs total; Table 2, p. 15): full agentic + blockchain digital twin configuration achieves mean anomaly detection latency of 3,197 s (vs. 39,374 s rule-based baseline), mitigation success rate of 66.2% (vs. 45.5% baseline), blockchain-anchored decision justification of 71.8% (vs. 0% baseline), and operator workload reduction of 91.7% (Abstract, p. 1; Section 6.4, pp. 15–18, Tables 2–3).
Exposed_Security_Function: Blockchain-anchored decision justification logging, smart-contract actuation gating, and multi-agent cross-verification.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Evaluated entirely in a simulated smart-city digital twin environment (N = 30 runs/config) without live physical SCADA telemetry, live LLM hallucination stress testing, or production permissioned blockchain network jitter (Section 7, p. 22).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1) & Section 6.4 (pp. 15–18, Tables 2–3): Evaluasi 5 konfigurasi (N=30 run per konfigurasi) menunjukkan penurunan latensi deteksi rata-rata dari 39.374 detik menjadi 3.197 detik, peningkatan keberhasilan mitigasi dari 45,5% ke 66,2%, justifikasi keputusan terjangkar blockchain sebesar 71,8%, dan reduksi beban kerja operator 91,7%.
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Integrates multi-agent digital twins with a permissioned blockchain for smart-city infrastructure, achieving 3,197 s mean detection latency (vs. 39,374 s baseline), 66.2% mitigation success, 71.8% blockchain-anchored decision justification, and 91.7% workload reduction.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Ablation simulation across 5 configurations (N = 30 runs each) for civil infrastructure digital twin management.
Protected_Object: Civil infrastructure SCADA actuation commands, sensor telemetry histories, and municipal audit trails.
Composition_Evidence: Ablation across 5 configurations isolates the additive contribution of multi-agent coordination (B2), digital-twin simulation gating (B3), and permissioned blockchain audit anchoring (B4) (Table 2, p. 15).
Coding_Rationale: Studi simulasi multi-agen + permissioned blockchain (PLOS One 2026, Stream M_AND_A) dengan studi ablasi 5 konfigurasi x 30 run yang sangat terukur (RQ3).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2; siap untuk rekonsiliasi dengan REVIEWER_1).

Study_Title: Agentic CDNs: A Multi-Agent Architecture for Edge-Native AI Inference and Control
Threat_Attacker_Model: Edge data privacy leakage across multi-tenant CDN nodes, Byzantine/malicious edge agent coordination, inference result tampering, and regulatory compliance violations (GDPR, CCPA, PDPA).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Agentic CDN Framework (ACF) combining a Permissioned Blockchain for verifiable inter-agent coordination, Secure Multi-Party Computation (SMPC), Differential Privacy (DP), and Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs) for verifiable edge AI inference.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Distributed Edge CDN Agent Nodes and Permissioned Blockchain Consensus/Verification Layer (Figures 1–3, pp. 1–3).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Privacy-preserving collaborative edge inference, cryptographic verifiability of edge computation via ZKPs, and tamper-evident multi-agent coordination.
Trust_Assumptions: Threshold honesty among SMPC/blockchain edge nodes and locally enforced DP noise calibration.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated across synthetic (~1.2M users across 12 edge regions) and public traces (Netflix, YouTube UGC, CAIDA): reduces end-to-end inference latency by 41.2%, increases cache hit rate by 34.8%, achieves 99.3% service availability and 96% coordination efficiency, and reduces backbone bandwidth usage by 62% (Abstract, p. 1; Sections V–VI, pp. 3–5, Figures 4–8).
Exposed_Security_Function: ZKP-verified edge inference, SMPC + DP collaborative telemetry aggregation, and permissioned blockchain coordination.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: High computational overhead of combining SMPC and ZKPs on resource-constrained edge nodes is noted as a key limitation (Section VIII, p. 6); quantum-resistant cryptography is mentioned only as future work (Section VII, p. 5).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1) & Sections IV–VIII (pp. 2–6, Figures 1–8): Agentic CDN Framework (ACF) menggabungkan permissioned blockchain, SMPC, Differential Privacy, dan ZKP pada 12 region edge (~1,2 juta pengguna), menurunkan latensi inferensi 41,2%, meningkatkan cache hit rate 34,8%, efisiensi koordinasi 96%, dan mengidentifikasi overhead komputasi SMPC+ZKP serta kriptografi tahan-kuantum sebagai agenda lanjutan.
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Agentic CDN Framework (ACF) integrates permissioned blockchain, SMPC, Differential Privacy, and ZKPs across edge LLM agents, reducing inference latency by 41.2% and backbone bandwidth by 62% with 96% coordination efficiency.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Multi-region edge CDN simulation (~1.2M users, 12 regions, Netflix/YouTube/CAIDA traces).
Protected_Object: Edge user request graphs, collaborative inference models, and inter-agent CDN routing decisions.
Composition_Evidence: Combines SMPC+DP telemetry aggregation and ZKP inference proofs (B3) with permissioned blockchain inter-agent coordination and audit logging (B2/B4) (Figure 3, p. 3).
Coding_Rationale: Studi Stream M pada edge CDN yang menggabungkan blockchain, SMPC, DP, dan ZKP serta menyebutkan kriptografi tahan-kuantum sebagai arah masa depan (STAGE_1_SUGGESTED_MIGRATION).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2; siap untuk rekonsiliasi dengan REVIEWER_1).

Study_Title: Agentic Cybersecurity: Autonomous Threat Detection Defense Against Adversarial Metamorphic Malware Attacks
Threat_Attacker_Model: Adversarial metamorphic malware (>95% code mutation rates across Virut, Zperm, Regswap, Evol, G2) attempting to evade signature scanners, plus inter-agent message spoofing, replay, tampering, and future Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later (HNDL) quantum attacks.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Cryptographically secured multi-agent ReAct architecture using Ed25519 digital signatures for agent authentication, ECDHE ephemeral key exchange, AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption with monotonic sequence numbers/timestamps for inter-agent channels, and behavioral invariant extraction (Algorithm 2).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Inter-Agent Cryptographic Messaging Layer and Sandboxed Behavioral Analysis Engine (Figures 1–2, pp. 2–4).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Authenticated and confidential inter-agent threat intelligence sharing, replay resistance, and high-recall behavioral detection of mutated malware families.
Trust_Assumptions: Agent private Ed25519 keys and behavioral sandbox telemetry collectors are isolated from the analyzed malware samples.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated on 2,847 metamorphic malware samples across 5 families: reaches 94.2% accuracy, 93.8% precision, 94.7% recall, and 0.942 F1 on known families (vs. 8.7% recall for ClamAV and 14.2% for YARA; Table V, p. 6), while Leave-One-Family-Out (LOFO) recall drops to 76.2% on unseen families (Abstract, p. 1; Sections V–VII, pp. 4–7, Tables V–VI).
Exposed_Security_Function: Ed25519 + ECDHE + AES-256-GCM inter-agent channel protection and multi-agent ReAct behavioral invariant extraction.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Recall drops from 94.7% to 76.2% under Leave-One-Family-Out (LOFO) evaluation on unseen families; Section V.E (p. 4) explicitly analyzes that ECDHE and Ed25519 fall to Shor's algorithm (while AES-256-GCM retains ~128-bit security under Grover's) and proposes migrating to ML-KEM (Kyber) and ML-DSA (Dilithium) against Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later threats.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1), Section V.E (p. 4, Positioning and Post-Quantum Considerations: analisis Shor/Grover pada ECDHE, Ed25519, AES-256-GCM dan migrasi ke ML-KEM/ML-DSA), serta Section VII (pp. 5–7, Tables V–VI): Arsitektur multi-agen terenkripsi (Ed25519 + AES-256-GCM) mencapai akurasi 94,2% (F1 0,942) pada 2.847 sampel malware metamorfik (recall 76,2% pada keluarga tak terlihat/LOFO).
Claim_Text_As_Reported: A multi-agent ReAct cybersecurity architecture secured with Ed25519, ECDHE, and AES-256-GCM achieves 94.2% accuracy (94.7% known-family recall, 76.2% LOFO unseen-family recall) on 2,847 metamorphic malware samples and analyzes post-quantum migration under Shor and Grover.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Pilot benchmark on 2,847 metamorphic samples across 5 families with explicit LOFO generalization bounds and formal post-quantum threat analysis.
Protected_Object: Inter-agent threat intelligence messages, behavioral invariant signatures, and SOC response actions.

Study_Title: Agentic LLM-Assisted Rotation Policies for Multi-Cloud Credential Management: A Systems Case Study With. NET 8, Zero-Knowledge Vault, and Terraform
Threat_Attacker_Model: Plaintext secret leakage into LLM prompts, git repositories, or Terraform state files; prompt-injection/jailbreak attacks inducing unsafe credential rotation policies; and service downtime during multi-cloud secret rotation.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Zero-Knowledge Managed Vault (single source of truth keeping raw secret values outside LLM/Terraform state; only cryptographic secret references/handles traverse the orchestrator) integrated with a .NET 8 lifecycle manager, OWASP/NIST policy guardrails, and formal zero-downtime add-then-remove rotation (Lemma 1).
Enforcement_Point_Location: .NET 8 Credential Lifecycle Manager & Zero-Knowledge Vault Reference Boundary prior to AWS/Azure Terraform projection (Figures 1–2, pp. 2–3).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Secret-value non-exposure invariant (raw secrets never enter LLM context or IaC state), bounded-failure availability <= sum(p^(k+1)) (Lemma 1), and guardrail suppression of unsafe LLM policy suggestions.
Trust_Assumptions: Managed Zero-Knowledge Vault, cloud IAM APIs (AWS/Azure), and .NET 8 deterministic policy store guardrails are trusted; advisory NLP/LLM layer is treated as untrusted.

Exposed_Security_Function: Vault-handle secret indirection, zero-downtime add-then-remove credential rotation, and OWASP/NIST guardrail validation of LLM policy synthesis.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Guardrails reduce but do not completely eliminate unsafe advisory suggestions (residual 2.6% unsafe suggestion rate and 1.1% jailbreak success in Table V, p. 4), requiring human/deterministic gate approval.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1), Section IV (p. 2, Lemma 1 Availability under Bounded Failures), dan Section IX (pp. 3–5, Tables III–VII): Sistem .NET 8 + Zero-Knowledge Vault + Terraform memangkas waktu rotasi armada 6 VM dari ~30 menit menjadi ~4 menit, mencapai F1 0,87 pada penemuan rahasia, serta menurunkan saran tidak aman dari 17,9% ke 2,6% dan keberhasilan jailbreak dari 12,4% ke 1,1%.
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Integrates a .NET 8 lifecycle manager, Zero-Knowledge Vault secret references, and OWASP/NIST guardrails for LLM-assisted multi-cloud credential rotation, cutting 6-VM rotation time from ~30 to ~4 minutes and reducing jailbreak success from 12.4% to 1.1%.

Protected_Object: Multi-cloud API tokens, SSH keys, database passwords, and Terraform state files.
Composition_Evidence: Isolates advisory LLM policy synthesis (B1) from deterministic .NET 8 / Zero-Knowledge Vault execution and Terraform projection (B3) with auditable rotation logs (B4) (Figures 1–2, pp. 2–3).

Study_Title: AgentLeak: A Benchmark for Internal-Channel Privacy Leakage in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
Threat_Attacker_Model: Internal-channel privacy leakage across seven multi-agent communication pathways (`C1` final output, `C2` inter-agent messages, `C3` tool arguments, `C4` tool outputs, `C5` shared memory/scratchpad, `C6` planning traces, `C7` logs) under both benign coordination and indirect prompt injection.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (AgentLeak benchmark instrumenting 7 internal/external multi-agent channels with contextual-integrity privacy auditing and evaluation of selective disclosure / sanitization defenses).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Multi-Agent Orchestration Bus, Shared Memory Scratchpad, and Inter-Agent Messaging Channels (`C1`–`C7`, Figure 1, p. 5).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Quantifies the internal-vs-external privacy audit gap in multi-agent LLM systems, proving that output-only (`C1`) audits miss the majority of internal-channel (`C2`, `C5`) contextual integrity violations.
Trust_Assumptions: Benchmark instruments orchestrator message buses and memory stores across CrewAI, AutoGen, LangGraph, and MetaGPT.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Across 1,000 scenarios (healthcare, finance, legal, corporate), 5 production LLMs (GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Mistral Large, Llama 3.3 70B), and 4,979 validated execution traces: multi-agent mode reduces final-output leakage (`C1`: 27.2% vs. 43.2% in single-agent mode), but total system leakage reaches 68.9% when aggregating internal channels (`C1`, `C2`, `C5`), with inter-agent messages (`C2`) leaking at 68.8%—meaning output-only audits miss 41.7% of privacy violations (Abstract, p. 1; Sections III–VI, pp. 3–15, Tables 1–2, Figure 1).
Exposed_Security_Function: Seven-channel (`C1`–`C7`) multi-agent contextual integrity privacy leakage instrumentation and audit benchmark.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Full 4,979-trace evaluation focuses on `C1`, `C2`, and `C5`, while `C3`/`C6` are evaluated on targeted 100-trace samples per model and `C4`/`C7` via SDK case studies (Section VII, p. 17).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1) & Sections III–VI (pp. 3–15, Tables 1–2, Figure 1): Pada 1.000 skenario, 5 LLM produksi, dan 4.979 jejak eksekusi tervalidasi, kebocoran pesan antar-agen (C2) mencapai 68,8% (total agregat C1/C2/C5 68,9%) dibandingkan 27,2% pada output akhir (C1), sehingga audit yang hanya memeriksa output akhir melewatkan 41,7% pelanggaran privasi.
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Across 1,000 scenarios, 5 production LLMs, and 4,979 traces, AgentLeak shows that inter-agent messages (C2) leak sensitive data in 68.8% of runs versus 27.2% in final outputs (C1), causing output-only audits to miss 41.7% of violations.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Large-scale empirical benchmark (4,979 traces, 5 frontier LLMs, 4 orchestration frameworks, 4 domains) grounded in Nissenbaum's contextual integrity.
Protected_Object: Domain-sensitive PII, PHI, financial records, and privileged legal facts traversing internal multi-agent channels (`C1`–`C7`).
Composition_Evidence: Directly measures how decomposing a single agent into multi-agent handoffs (`B2`) and shared memory (`B4`) lowers external output leakage (`C1`) while amplifying internal inter-agent leakage (`C2` = 68.8%) (pp. 1, 8–15).
Coding_Rationale: Benchmark empiris berskala besar di IEEE Access 2026 (4.979 jejak eksekusi, Stream A) yang membuktikan celah kebocoran kanal internal multi-agen (68,8% pada C2 vs. 27,2% pada C1).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2; siap untuk rekonsiliasi dengan REVIEWER_1).

Study_Title: AI Agents in Industry 4.0: AASOPC UALLM Architecture as the Foundation of Intelligent Manufacturing Systems in the Context of Industrial Enterprise Implementation
Threat_Attacker_Model: Unsafe autonomous LLM actuation in safety-critical Industry 4.0 cyber-physical manufacturing systems, unauthorized OPC UA write commands, token tampering, and prompt-induced hallucinated parameters.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: AAS-OPC UA-LLM Architecture integrating a five-step Security Enforcement Module (SEM) that validates cryptographically signed JSON Web Tokens (JWTs), OPC UA security profiles (X.509 certificates / signed & encrypted channels), Asset Administration Shell (AAS) submodel capability bounds, physical safety invariants, and mandatory Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) cryptographic approval gates.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Five-Step Security Enforcement Module (SEM) & HITL Approval Gateway mediating between the LLM Agent and OPC UA / AAS Industrial Controllers (Figure 1, p. 13; Table 1, p. 7).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Non-bypassable five-step verification of industrial actuation commands, cryptographic JWT authorization binding, and mandatory human sign-off for safety-critical writes.
Trust_Assumptions: Industrial OPC UA PKI, SEM verification gateway, and human operator approval terminals are trusted.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated in two controlled laboratory proof-of-concept case studies (informed by an n = 117 industrial employee survey): automated system processing latency is 1.7 s for predictive maintenance (hydraulic pump overheat) and ~15 s for production scheduling, with end-to-end latencies (including mandatory HITL approval) of 14.9 s and 62 s respectively—representing 97% and 96% time reductions over manual workflows (Abstract, p. 1; Sections 3–5, pp. 4–25, Tables 1–2, Figure 1).
Exposed_Security_Function: Five-step SEM verification (signed JWT check, AAS schema validation, physical range check, HITL gate, OPC UA secure session execution).
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Validated under controlled laboratory proof-of-concept conditions rather than a live multi-line factory floor; mandatory HITL approval dominates end-to-end latency (14.9 s and 62 s vs. 1.7 s automated processing).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1) & Sections 3–5 (pp. 4–25, Tables 1–2, Figure 1): Arsitektur AAS–OPC UA–LLM menerapkan prosedur verifikasi 5 langkah pada Security Enforcement Module (SEM) menggunakan JWT bertanda tangan dan persetujuan wajib HITL, mencatat latensi pemrosesan sistem 1,7 detik (pemeliharaan) dan ~15 detik (penjadwalan), atau 14,9 detik dan 62 detik end-to-end termasuk persetujuan manusia (penghematan 97% dan 96%).
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Integrates AAS, OPC UA, and LLM agents with a five-step Security Enforcement Module (signed JWTs + mandatory HITL gating), achieving 1.7 s and ~15 s automated processing latencies (14.9 s and 62 s end-to-end with HITL).
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Industrial survey (n = 117) and two laboratory proof-of-concept manufacturing case studies (maintenance and scheduling).
Protected_Object: OPC UA industrial actuator commands, Asset Administration Shell (AAS) submodels, and shop-floor safety parameters.
Composition_Evidence: Chains LLM diagnostic reasoning and HITL approval (B1) with five-step SEM JWT/bounds verification and OPC UA actuation (B3) plus audit logging (B4) (Figure 1, p. 13).
Coding_Rationale: Studi prototipe sistem industri Stream M (32 halaman, MDPI Applied Sciences 2026) yang mengkombinasikan JWT, OPC UA, AAS, dan verifikasi 5 langkah SEM + HITL.

Study_Title: AI Agents Need Both Hardware-Backed Security and Application-Level Guardrails
Threat_Attacker_Model: Two-front adversary combining (1) application-level indirect prompt injection to exfiltrate sandboxed files and (2) infrastructure/host-level privilege compromise targeting agent memory, model weights, and guardrail configurations.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Hardware-backed Confidential Virtual Machines (CVMs, AMD SEV-SNP / Intel TDX) + Confidential GPUs with remote attestation combined with in-enclave application-level guardrails (`LlamaFirewall`: PromptGuard + AlignmentCheck + CodeShield).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Hardware-Attested Confidential VM / GPU Execution Boundary co-hosting the LLM Agent and `LlamaFirewall` Guardrail Pipeline (Figures 1–3, pp. 1–5).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Simultaneous protection against infrastructure memory/state snooping (via CVM hardware encryption/attestation) and semantic prompt injection/data exfiltration (via enclave-protected `LlamaFirewall` guardrails).
Trust_Assumptions: CPU/GPU TEE hardware roots of trust (AMD SEV-SNP / Intel TDX / NVIDIA H100 CC) are trusted; host hypervisor and external tool inputs are untrusted.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Deploying the agent and `LlamaFirewall` inside a Confidential VM incurs ~7% latency overhead compared to a standard non-confidential VM while preserving identical agent task utility and blocking prompt-injection file exfiltration (Section 4–5, pp. 2–5, Figures 1–3).
Exposed_Security_Function: Confidential VM/GPU memory isolation, remote attestation of guardrail integrity, and `LlamaFirewall` prompt/alignment/code inspection.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Preliminary system design and benchmark (SysTEX '26 workshop paper); `LlamaFirewall` alignment checks add sequential LLM guardrail latency on top of the 7% CVM overhead, and adaptive jailbreaks can still challenge probabilistic guardrails.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract & Sections 3–5 (pp. 1–5, Figures 1–3): Menggabungkan Confidential VM/GPU dengan guardrail tingkat aplikasi (`LlamaFirewall`) di dalam batas TEE yang teratestasi, menghasilkan overhead latensi hanya ~7% dibandingkan VM standar sembari mempertahankan utilitas agen dan mencegah eksfiltrasi data.
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Co-locates LLM agents and LlamaFirewall application guardrails inside hardware-backed Confidential VMs, incurring ~7% CVM latency overhead while defending against both host compromise and prompt injection.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Preliminary prototype benchmark comparing agent utility and LlamaFirewall latency across Confidential VMs and standard VMs.
Protected_Object: Sandboxed agent files, runtime memory/weights, and LlamaFirewall guardrail integrity.
Composition_Evidence: Demonstrates why hardware TEEs (protecting execution/audit integrity at B3/B4) and application guardrails (filtering prompt/tool injections at B1/B3) must be composed inside the same attested CVM (Figure 1, p. 1).
Coding_Rationale: Studi Stream M_AND_A (TU Munich & Huawei Munich, SysTEX '26) yang mengukur langsung komposisi Confidential VM + `LlamaFirewall` (overhead CVM ~7%, Figures 2–3, p. 5).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2; siap untuk rekonsiliasi dengan REVIEWER_1).

Study_Title: AI Agents with Decentralized Identifiers and Verifiable Credentials
Threat_Attacker_Model: Cross-domain agent impersonation, Sybil/untrusted peer dialogues, and unauthorized capability claims at the onset of Agent-to-Agent (A2A) interactions across organizational boundaries.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Self-Sovereign Identity (SSI) Multi-Agent Framework combining ledger-anchored W3C Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs), W3C Verifiable Credentials (VCs), and the Decentralized Identity Foundation (DIF) Presentation Exchange / Proof Protocol integrated into Google A2A agent dialogues.
Enforcement_Point_Location: A2A Agent Dialogue Handshake & SSI Wallet/Verifier Middleware (Figures 1–2, pp. 4–5).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Cryptographically verifiable cross-domain agent identity and third-party attested capability/affiliation verification prior to A2A task execution.
Trust_Assumptions: Distributed ledger anchoring DID documents and third-party VC issuers are trusted; LLM agents invoke SSI wallet verification tools correctly.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated across 3 multi-agent A2A processes (Processes I, II, III of increasing attestation complexity) and 4 OpenAI models (`GPT-4.1-mini`, `GPT-4o-mini`, `o4-mini`, `GPT-4.1`): `GPT-4.1` and `o4-mini` achieve 80%–91% process completion rates (vs. 4%–36% on smaller `mini` models in complex Process II/III; Figure 3, p. 6), with mean end-to-end completion times of 1–3.5 minutes dominated by LLM reasoning calls and token consumption (50k–180k tokens) rather than cryptographic DID/VC verification (Section 6, pp. 5–7, Figures 3–7).
Exposed_Security_Function: W3C DID resolution, DIF Verifiable Presentation request/verification, and A2A mutual trust handshake.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: When LLM agents orchestrate multi-step DIF presentation proofs autonomously via tool calls, smaller models (`GPT-4o-mini`, `GPT-4.1-mini`) fail frequently (completion rates dropping to 4%–13% in Process II), and end-to-end handshakes consume 1–3.5 minutes and up to 180k tokens (Figures 3–7, pp. 6–7).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Sections 4–6 (pp. 3–7, Figures 1–7): Mengintegrasikan W3C DID, Verifiable Credentials, dan protokol DIF Presentation Proof ke dalam dialog multi-agen A2A; evaluasi pada 4 model LLM menunjukkan tingkat penyelesaian 80%–91% pada `o4-mini`/`GPT-4.1` (namun turun hingga 4%–13% pada model `mini` untuk Proses II) dengan durasi rata-rata 1–3,5 menit dan konsumsi 50k–180k token.
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Equips A2A agents with W3C DIDs and Verifiable Credentials via the DIF Presentation Proof protocol, achieving 80%–91% cross-domain attestation completion on frontier models (`o4-mini`, `GPT-4.1`) across three multi-agent workflows.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Prototypical multi-agent SSI + A2A implementation benchmarked across 3 workflow complexities and 4 OpenAI models (`GPT-4.1-mini`, `GPT-4o-mini`, `o4-mini`, `GPT-4.1`).
Protected_Object: Agent long-lived digital identities (W3C DIDs), organizational attestations (VCs), and cross-domain A2A dialogues.
Composition_Evidence: Embeds W3C DID/VC presentation exchange directly inside A2A inter-agent negotiation dialogues (`B2`) and measures how LLM reasoning capability governs cryptographic protocol completion (Figures 2–7, pp. 5–7).
Coding_Rationale: Studi empiris sangat menarik dari TU Berlin (Stream M) yang mengukur tingkat keberhasilan, durasi (1–3,5 menit), dan konsumsi token (hingga 180k token) ketika agen LLM menjalankan protokol W3C DID/VC di atas A2A (RQ3).

Study_Title: An agentic AI marketplace for prelitigation analyses with ZKP-integrated ethical verifications

Enforcement_Point_Location: Decentralized Legal AI Marketplace Smart Contract, Smart Contract Oracle, and ZKP Verifier Gateway prior to agent selection (Figures 2–3, pp. 7, 13).

Trust_Assumptions: Registered accredited auditors signing dataset commitments via smart contract oracles are honest (or multi-auditor threshold holds) and underlying BBS+, Bulletproofs, and zk-SNARK cryptographic assumptions hold.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: NR (Eksplisit menyatakan pada Abstract p. 1 & Section 1 p. 2 bahwa studi ini menyajikan kerangka kerja konseptual dan arsitektural tanpa evaluasi performa sistem empiris; menyajikan pemetaan kompleksitas kualitatif antara BBS+, Bulletproofs, dan zk-SNARKs pada Table 2, p. 15).

Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Requires black-box query iterations against a surrogate or target LLM to optimize tool metadata attractiveness; increasing declared parameter counts beyond task relevance eventually lowers ASR on stronger models (Figure 5, p. 22).

Claim_Text_As_Reported: Attractive Metadata Attack (AMA) optimizes syntactically and semantically valid tool names, descriptions, and parameter schemas in a black-box setting, inducing LLM agents to invoke malicious tools at 81%–95% ASR.

Study_Title: AUDITRON: Secure AI-Orchestrated Auditing with Privilege-Gated Data Actions
Threat_Attacker_Model: Prompt injection, unauthorized attribute exposure (e.g., LLM-generated SQL JOINs surfacing hidden PII columns), and privilege escalation during AI-orchestrated enterprise financial/compliance auditing.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: AUDITRON layered control architecture isolating the LLM to intent classification and parameter extraction only, while a server-side Model Context Protocol (MCP) Privilege Policy Engine enforces deterministic RBAC/ABAC across 4 distinct roles and a Model Context Operator (MCO) executes parameterized SQL/CSV/PDF API calls with tamper-evident audit logging.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Server-side MCP Privilege Policy Engine & MCO Secure API Gateway isolating the LLM from direct database schema/credential access (Figure 1 & Algorithm 1, p. 3505 / PDF p. 4).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Strict separation of language understanding from execution authority, 100% RBAC/ABAC privilege enforcement (zero direct LLM SQL/DB access), and complete tamper-evident logging of authorized and denied actions.
Trust_Assumptions: User authentication/role assignment system, server-side MCP/MCO modules, and underlying parameterized DB adapter are trusted; LLM output is treated as untrusted.

Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Evaluated on a small mock banking database (1,000–1,100 records, 20 queries) rather than multi-million-row production warehouses; relies on classical RBAC/ABAC without cryptographic capability tokens or training-time poisoning defenses (Section 2.3, p. 3504 & Section 4.2, p. 3506).
