Study_Title: Authenticated and Offline-Verifiable Agent-to-Agent Messaging for LLM Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Prompt-injection-induced message forgery, sender repudiation, log tampering/equivocation by untrusted logging servers, and lack of online PKI/registry connectivity during forensic verification of Agent-to-Agent (A2A) workflows.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Offline-Verifiable Proof-Carrying A2A Receipt Bundle combining RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS), Ed25519 client message signatures, SHA-256 binary Merkle tree inclusion proofs, Ed25519-signed periodic Signed Tree Heads (STH), and an embedded minimal W3C DID registry snapshot for offline public-key resolution.
Enforcement_Point_Location: A2A Messaging Server Merkle Logger and Standalone Offline Third-Party Receipt Verifier (Figures 1–3, Table I, pp. 2–5).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Non-repudiable message authorship, tamper-evident log inclusion (O(log N) Merkle proof), and 100% self-contained offline verification without contacting sender, receiver, or online PKI.
Trust_Assumptions: Agent Ed25519 signing keys and the initial snapshot of the minimal DID registry are authentic; periodic STH checkpoints prevent silent server history rewrites.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Merkle inclusion proof size scales logarithmically as O(log N); on the test platform, median standalone offline verification time across all four cryptographic checks (payload hash match, client Ed25519 signature, Merkle inclusion path, and STH Ed25519 signature) is ~0.4 s with compact JSON receipt bundles (Abstract, p. 1; Section V, pp. 4–6, Figures 1–3, Tables I–III).
Exposed_Security_Function: RFC 8785 JCS canonicalization, Ed25519 message & STH signing, SHA-256 Merkle inclusion proof generation, and offline 4-step bundle verification.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: STH issuance is serialized per checkpoint (concurrent inserts wait for the next checkpoint); relies on pre-quantum Ed25519 signatures and does not prevent an authorized agent from signing a prompt-injected semantic payload.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1) & Sections II–V (pp. 2–6, Figures 1–3, Tables I–III): Memperkenalkan tanda terima A2A pembawa-bukti (proof-carrying receipt) berbasis RFC 8785 JCS, tanda tangan Ed25519, bukti inklusi pohon Merkle O(log N), Signed Tree Head (STH), dan registri DID minimal dengan median waktu verifikasi luring (offline) ~0,4 detik.
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Provides authenticated, offline-verifiable proof-carrying receipts for A2A messaging using RFC 8785 JCS, Ed25519 signatures, Merkle inclusion proofs, Signed Tree Heads, and embedded DID snapshots with ~0.4 s median offline verification time.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Prototype HTTP A2A logging server and offline verifier benchmarked for latency, O(log N) receipt size, and verification time.
Protected_Object: A2A inter-agent JSON messages, authorship signatures, and append-only audit log histories.
Composition_Evidence: Binds live inter-agent A2A message authentication (`B2`) directly to self-contained offline forensic audit bundles (`B4`) via Merkle inclusion proofs and STH checkpoints (Figures 1 & 3, pp. 3, 5).
Coding_Rationale: Studi Stream M_AND_A yang sangat konkret mengimplementasikan tanda terima kriptografi luring (RFC 8785 JCS + Ed25519 + Merkle proof + STH + DID) untuk pesan A2A dengan verifikasi luring ~0,4 detik.
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2; siap untuk rekonsiliasi dengan REVIEWER_1).

Study_Title: Automatic Red Teaming LLM-Based Agents With Model Context Protocol Tools
Threat_Attacker_Model: Automated red-teaming adversary (`AutoMalTool`) generating stealthy malicious MCP tools that poison tool descriptions, manipulate tool-invocation parameters, or corrupt output interpretation across mainstream LLM agents.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (`AutoMalTool` four-stage automated red-teaming pipeline: Initial Generator, Oracle, Effectiveness Evaluator, and feedback-driven Tool Optimizer; evaluated against `MCP-Scan` and `A.I.G` scanners).
Enforcement_Point_Location: MCP Tool Description & Output Ingestion Interface across LLM Agents and Static/Black-box MCP Security Scanners (Figures 1–2, pp. 3–4).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Demonstrates that automated feedback-optimized malicious MCP tools achieve high generation/attack success while evading state-of-the-art MCP vulnerability scanners.
Trust_Assumptions: Attacker can publish or register MCP tools into the agent's candidate toolset and observe task-level feedback during red-team optimization.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated across mainstream LLM agents and three MCP server ecosystems: `AutoMalTool` achieves ~85.0% average malicious tool generation success rate and 35.3% effective end-to-end attack success rate (ASR), completing optimization within 200 seconds and <$0.05 financial token cost per malicious MCP tool (Fig. 3, p. 10), while reducing detection rates of existing scanners to 11.1% on `MCP-Scan` and 23.4% on `A.I.G` (Section I, p. 2; Sections IV–V, pp. 6–11).

Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract & Section I (pp. 1–2), Section II–III (pp. 2–5, Figures 1–2), dan Section IV (pp. 6–11, Figure 3): `AutoMalTool` mencapai rata-rata keberhasilan pembuatan alat MCP berbahaya 85,0% dan ASR efektif 35,3% dalam waktu <200 detik per alat, sementara deteksi pemindai keamanan hanya mencapai 11,1% pada `MCP-Scan` dan 23,4% pada `A.I.G`.
Claim_Text_As_Reported: AutoMalTool automatically generates malicious MCP tools with an 85.0% generation success rate and 35.3% effective ASR within 200 seconds per tool, evading MCP-Scan (11.1% detection) and A.I.G (23.4% detection).
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Extensive automated red-teaming benchmark across mainstream LLM agents, three MCP server suites, and two industrial MCP scanners (MCP-Scan, A.I.G).

Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Secure Agent Workflow (SAW) Zero-Trust Platform combining mutual TLS (mTLS), short-lived cryptographic identity tokens, continuous risk-adaptive Policy Enforcement Point (PEP) mediation, sandboxed tool execution, and append-only cryptographic hash-chained audit logs.

Claim_Text_As_Reported: Secure Agent Workflow (SAW) embeds zero-trust identity management, continuous policy enforcement, and tamper-proof logging into the agent runtime, improving malicious action detection with modest latency overhead across 10 simulation runs.

Study_Title: Balancing Security and Performance in LLM Agents: Spotlight-Guard, a Layered Defense Against Indirect Prompt Injection
Threat_Attacker_Model: Non-adaptive and adaptive Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) attacks embedded in external tool outputs (web pages, emails, files, APIs) attempting to hijack locally hosted 7B-class open-weight LLM agents (`Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct`, `Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct`, `Mistral-7B-Instruct`).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Spotlight-Guard Layered Defense combining (1) Spotlighting-based cryptographic/delimited input isolation, (2) an LLM detection-and-quarantine pipeline, and (3) HMAC-SHA256 (Hash-based Message Authentication Code) instruction integrity verification binding system instructions and delimiter tokens.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Agent Tool-Output Ingestion & Prompt Assembly Pipeline prior to LLM tool-invocation reasoning (Sections 3–4, pp. 9–18, Table 1).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Cryptographic instruction/delimiter integrity via HMAC and layered quarantine of indirect prompt injections while preserving benign task utility.
Trust_Assumptions: Per-session HMAC secret key generated by the host orchestrator remains inaccessible to untrusted external tool outputs.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals across locally hosted 7B-class models: full Spotlight-Guard reduces Indirect Prompt Injection ASR from 36.0% to 17.2% (and down to 6.7% ASR under adaptive pipeline-targeted attacks) while preserving a 97.2% benign-task success rate and raising detection F1 from 0.749 to 0.892, at the cost of additional quarantine LLM invocations per flagged request (Abstract, p. 1; Sections 4–5, pp. 18–29, Table 1).
Exposed_Security_Function: HMAC-authenticated spotlighting delimiters, LLM injection detection & quarantine, and context integrity verification.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Leaves a residual 17.2% ASR (6.7% under adaptive pipeline attacks) on 7B-class models because valid HMAC tags guarantee delimiter origin integrity but cannot stop the LLM attention mechanism from semantically attending to quarantined text if detection misses.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1) & Sections 3–5 (pp. 9–29, Table 1): Spotlight-Guard menggabungkan isolasi input spotlighting, pipeline deteksi-dan-karantina LLM, serta verifikasi integritas instruksi berbasis HMAC pada model open-weight kelas 7B, menurunkan ASR dari 36,0% menjadi 17,2% (6,7% pada serangan adaptif), mempertahankan 97,2% keberhasilan tugas jinak, dan meningkatkan F1 deteksi dari 0,749 ke 0,892.
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Spotlight-Guard combines spotlighting input isolation, LLM detection-and-quarantine, and HMAC instruction integrity on 7B-class agents, reducing IPI ASR from 36.0% to 17.2% (6.7% adaptive) while preserving 97.2% benign task success and 0.892 detection F1.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Comprehensive 34-page testbed evaluation with bootstrap 95% CIs across locally hosted 7B-class open-weight LLM agents.
Protected_Object: System instructions, spotlighting delimiter boundaries, and external tool-output ingestion streams.
Composition_Evidence: Composes HMAC cryptographic instruction/delimiter authentication at prompt assembly (`B1`) with LLM detection-and-quarantine over inbound external tool outputs (`B3`) (pp. 1, 12–25).
Coding_Rationale: Studi komprehensif 34 halaman (MDPI Applied Sciences 2026, Stream M_AND_A) yang menggabungkan HMAC instruction integrity dengan spotlighting dan karantina LLM (ASR 36,0% -> 17,2%, benign utility 97,2%, F1 0,892).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2; siap untuk rekonsiliasi dengan REVIEWER_1).

Study_Title: Benchmarking MCP Vulnerability Detection from a Paired Evaluation Perspective
Threat_Attacker_Model: Vulnerable MCP server code implementations containing Remote Code Execution (RCE), Sensitive Information Disclosure, Insecure File Operations, and SQL/Command Injection flaws that static/LLM scanners fail to distinguish from patched fixes.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (`PairedMCPVul` benchmark comprising 75 paired vulnerable and fixed MCP server tools evaluated using the Matched Pair Accuracy MPA metric across LLM detectors and static analyzers).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Pre-deployment MCP Server Code Auditing & Vulnerability Detection Pipeline (Figure 1, Tables 1–2, pp. 3–4).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Quantifies whether vulnerability scanners semantically distinguish vulnerable MCP server code from its patched counterpart rather than triggering on superficial API keywords.
Trust_Assumptions: Benchmark evaluates 75 manually cross-validated Python MCP tool pairs covering 95% of the dominant language in the MCP ecosystem.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Across 75 paired vulnerable/fixed MCP tools (150 tools total; Table 1–2, pp. 3–4) evaluating `Claude Haiku-4.5`, `DeepSeek V3.2`, `GPT-5-mini`, `Bandit`, `Semgrep`, and `AI-Infra-Guard`: `Claude Haiku-4.5` achieves the highest Matched Pair Accuracy (MPA) of 0.853, whereas `GPT-5-mini` attains 0.842 F1 but only 0.653 MPA, and static tools (`Bandit`, `Semgrep`, `AI-Infra-Guard`) suffer low MPA due to high false positives on fixed code (Abstract, p. 1; Section 3, pp. 4–5, Table 2).
Exposed_Security_Function: Paired vulnerable-vs-fixed MCP server vulnerability benchmarking (`PairedMCPVul`) and Matched Pair Accuracy (`MPA`) evaluation.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Benchmark is synthesized via Gemini-1.5-Pro (with manual cross-validation) and limited to 75 Python MCP tool pairs (excluding TypeScript/Go MCP servers).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1) & Sections 2–3 (pp. 2–5, Figure 1, Tables 1–2): Pada benchmark `PairedMCPVul` (75 pasang alat MCP rentan dan telah diperbaiki), `Claude Haiku-4.5` mencapai Matched Pair Accuracy (MPA) tertinggi sebesar 0,853, sedangkan `GPT-5-mini` mencapai F1 0,842 namun hanya 0,653 MPA, membuktikan bahwa metrik F1 konvensional melebih-lebihkan kemampuan deteksi.
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Introduces PairedMCPVul (75 paired vulnerable and fixed MCP tools) and shows that while GPT-5-mini achieves 0.842 F1, its Matched Pair Accuracy (MPA) is only 0.653 (vs. 0.853 MPA for Claude Haiku-4.5).
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Paired evaluation benchmark of 6 detectors (3 LLMs: Claude Haiku-4.5, DeepSeek V3.2, GPT-5-mini; 3 SAST tools: Bandit, Semgrep, AI-Infra-Guard) across 75 MCP tool pairs.
Protected_Object: MCP server tool source code across RCE, Sensitive Information Disclosure, and Insecure File Operation categories.
Composition_Evidence: Demonstrates that static keyword matching on MCP tool execution APIs (`B3`) yields severe false positives on patched code unless semantic control/data-flow checks are performed (Table 2, p. 3).
Coding_Rationale: Studi benchmark FSE Companion '26 (Stream A) yang memperkenalkan `PairedMCPVul` (75 pasang alat MCP) dan metrik MPA untuk menguji detektor kerentanan MCP.
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2; siap untuk rekonsiliasi dengan REVIEWER_1).

Study_Title: Beyond Detection: Autonomous Anomaly Remediation for MCP Against Tool Poisoning Attacks
Threat_Attacker_Model: MCP Tool Poisoning Attacks (TPA) in web-automation and tool-augmented agents (>70% baseline ASR) that corrupt agent reasoning and hijack tool invocation trajectories.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (`MCPFixGen`: autonomous anomaly detection and remediation framework combining selective inspection triggering, multi-feature behavioral abnormality detection, and a multi-checkpoint state rollback & context remediation mechanism).
Enforcement_Point_Location: MCP Agent Execution Monitor & Multi-Checkpoint Rollback Engine between the LLM Planner and MCP Tool Servers (Figure 1, p. 2).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Automated real-time detection of tool-poisoning trajectory deviations and autonomous state rollback/remediation without aborting benign user tasks.
Trust_Assumptions: Host checkpoint manager can snapshot and roll back local agent state/context before irreversible external side effects occur.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated on `MCPTox` (poisoned) and `ToolACE` (benign) across `Qwen3-8B`, `Qwen3-14B`, and frontier models (Table 2, p. 7): reduces inspection trigger rate to <13% of steps, slashes Tool Poisoning Attack Success Rate (ASR) to <0.3% (e.g., from 38.8% to 0.0% on `Qwen3-8B` and from 21.1% to 0.1% on `Qwen3-14B`), boosts Task Completion Rate (TCR) under attack from 61.2% to 89.1% (`Qwen3-8B`), and adds only 0.5–2.1 s average time overhead per task (Abstract, p. 1; Section 4, pp. 5–8, Table 2).
Exposed_Security_Function: Selective anomaly inspection triggering (<13% rate), multi-checkpoint state rollback, and automated tool-context remediation (`MCPFixGen`).
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Multi-checkpoint rollback requires external tool actions to be idempotent or reversible; non-rollbackable external side effects (e.g., already transmitted network packets/emails) cannot be undone post-execution.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1) & Sections 3–4 (pp. 3–8, Figure 1, Tables 1–2): `MCPFixGen` menekan laju pemicuan inspeksi di bawah 13%, menurunkan ASR Tool Poisoning Attack hingga <0,3% (38,8% -> 0,0% pada Qwen3-8B; 21,1% -> 0,1% pada Qwen3-14B), serta meningkatkan penyelesaian tugas (TCR) dari 61,2% menjadi 89,1% dengan tambahan waktu hanya 0,5–2,1 detik.
Claim_Text_As_Reported: MCPFixGen autonomously detects and remediates MCP tool poisoning via selective inspection (<13% trigger rate) and multi-checkpoint rollback, reducing TPA ASR to <0.3% and raising task completion from 61.2% to 89.1%.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Controlled benchmark on MCPTox (poisoned) and ToolACE (benign) across multiple LLM backbones (WWW '26).
Protected_Object: MCP agent reasoning state, tool invocation trajectories, and web-automation task completion.
Composition_Evidence: Couples selective runtime anomaly inspection at tool invocation (`B3`) with multi-checkpoint state rollback and context repair (`B4`) across multi-step MCP workflows (Figure 1, p. 2; Table 2, p. 7).
Coding_Rationale: Studi WWW '26 (Stream A) yang memperkenalkan remediasi otonom `MCPFixGen` berbasis multi-checkpoint rollback terhadap Tool Poisoning Attacks (ASR <0,3%, pemicuan inspeksi <13%).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2; siap untuk rekonsiliasi dengan REVIEWER_1).

Study_Title: Beyond the Protocol: Unveiling Attack Vectors in the Model Context Protocol (MCP) Ecosystem
Threat_Attacker_Model: Malicious MCP server adversary launching four end-to-end ecosystem attack classes: (1) Tool Poisoning Attacks (TPA), (2) Puppet Attacks (cross-server shadowing/hijacking), (3) Rug Pull Attacks (post-installation dynamic mutation), and (4) Exploitation via Malicious External Resources.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (End-to-end empirical attack surface evaluation across 4 attack vectors, an Controlled User Study with 20 developers/users on a simulated MCP marketplace of 13 servers, and an automated static/LLM scanner audit across real-world MCP repositories).
Enforcement_Point_Location: MCP Marketplace Discovery, Client Installation, and Multi-Server Runtime Tool Invocation Boundaries (Figures 1–5, pp. 3–6).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Demonstrates end-to-end exploitability of all four MCP attack classes (including private file exfiltration `/Users/thirdpc/test/env.md` and financial/result manipulation) and high human susceptibility during server selection.
Trust_Assumptions: Users discover and install third-party MCP servers alongside benign privileged servers (e.g., `Desktop Commander`) within the same MCP host.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: In the 20-participant user study (90% with SE/AI experience) over a simulated MCP platform where 4 of 13 servers were malicious, 75.0% (15/20) selected at least one malicious MCP server even when warned; end-to-end experiments across mainstream LLMs confirm high ASR for TPA, Puppet, Rug Pull, and External Resource attacks (Sections 3–5, pp. 3–18, Figures 1–5, Table 3).
Exposed_Security_Function: Four-vector MCP attack surface taxonomy (TPA, Puppet, Rug Pull, External Resource) and empirical human/LLM vulnerability evaluation.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: User study cohort is limited to 20 participants on a 13-server simulated marketplace; highlights the lack of cryptographic code-signing, version pinning, and cross-server capability isolation in standard MCP hosts.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract & Sections 3–4 (pp. 1, 3–12, Figures 1–5, Table 3): Mengidentifikasi dan mengevaluasi empat vektor serangan ekosistem MCP (Tool Poisoning, Puppet Attack, Rug Pull, dan Malicious External Resources) serta studi pengguna (N=20, 90% berpengalaman SE/AI) di mana 75,0% (15/20) tetap memilih setidaknya satu server MCP berbahaya.
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Unveils and empirically validates four MCP ecosystem attack vectors (Tool Poisoning, Puppet, Rug Pull, and Malicious External Resources), showing that 75.0% of experienced participants install malicious MCP servers in a controlled user study.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: End-to-end empirical evaluation across four attack classes and a 20-participant developer user study (IEEE TSE 2026).
Protected_Object: Local sensitive files (`/Users/thirdpc/test/env.md`), sibling MCP servers (`Desktop Commander`), and agent tool outputs.
Composition_Evidence: Demonstrates cross-server composition in Puppet and TPA attacks where a benign-looking `weather_forecast` MCP server induces the agent to invoke the privileged `Desktop Commander` server (`B2`/`B3`) and exfiltrate local environment files (`B4`) (p. 23).
Coding_Rationale: Studi empiris IEEE TSE 2026 (Stream A) yang memetakan 4 vektor serangan ekosistem MCP (TPA, Puppet, Rug Pull, External Resources) beserta studi pengguna (75% terinfeksi).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2; siap untuk rekonsiliasi dengan REVIEWER_1).

Study_Title: Beyond Tool Poisoning: Attack Surfaces of Malicious Remote MCP Servers Across LLM Platforms
Threat_Attacker_Model: Anonymous malicious remote MCP server operator exploiting the full remote server surface across two axes: `LLM-passive` attacks (executing inside the remote server: credential harvesting, image steganography exfiltration) and `LLM-active` attacks (requiring host LLM participation: phishing link insertion, malicious code augmentation, cross-tool data exfiltration).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (Cross-platform empirical benchmark measuring Attack Success Rate ASR and Self-Reporting Rate SRR across three commercial MCP hosts: Claude Desktop, ChatGPT, and Gemini CLI/host).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Remote MCP Server SSE/HTTP Endpoint and Commercial LLM Host Client Interface (Figure 1, p. 4; Table 1, p. 9).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Reveals sharp cross-platform divergence in LLM-active attack resistance and near-zero user self-reporting (0% SRR) for LLM-passive remote MCP server attacks.
Trust_Assumptions: User connects a remote third-party MCP server via URL to commercial hosts (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini) under standard platform permissions.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated across five attack scenarios on Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini (Table 1, p. 9; Sections 4–5, pp. 9–18): credential-bearing email exfiltration varies sharply across platforms (95% ASR on Claude vs. 50% ASR on ChatGPT), whereas channel-optimized attacks succeed across all three platforms at ASR >= 85%; critically, the Self-Reporting Rate (SRR) is 0% across all LLM-passive attacks (and most active attacks except code augmentation where LLM self-reports in 100% of runs), leaving users unaware of compromise (Abstract, pp. 1–3; Sections 4–5, pp. 8–18).
Exposed_Security_Function: Two-axis remote MCP threat taxonomy (`LLM-passive` vs. `LLM-active`) and cross-platform ASR + Self-Reporting Rate (`SRR`) benchmarking.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Evaluated on three commercial LLM hosts at a fixed point in time; shows that host-side prompt guardrails cannot observe or prevent `LLM-passive` attacks that complete entirely inside a remote MCP server.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract & Section 1 (pp. 1–3), Section 3–4 (pp. 4–9, Figure 1, Table 1), dan Section 5 (pp. 10–18): Mengevaluasi 5 skenario serangan server MCP jarak jauh (`LLM-passive` vs. `LLM-active`) pada Claude, ChatGPT, dan Gemini; mencatat divergensi tajam antar-platform (95% ASR pada Claude vs. 50% pada ChatGPT untuk permintaan email berkredensial), ASR >= 85% pada saluran teroptimasi, dan Self-Reporting Rate (SRR) 0% pada seluruh serangan pasif-LLM.
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Evaluates five LLM-passive and LLM-active attack scenarios from malicious remote MCP servers across Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini, finding 95% vs. 50% cross-platform ASR divergence, >=85% channel-optimized ASR, and 0% Self-Reporting Rate (SRR) on all LLM-passive attacks.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Cross-platform empirical evaluation on production MCP hosts (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini) across 5 attack scenarios.
Protected_Object: User credentials, uploaded files/images, generated code integrity, and host user awareness (`SRR`).
Composition_Evidence: Demonstrates how delegating tool execution to a remote MCP URL (`B3`) allows `LLM-passive` exfiltration and `LLM-active` response manipulation (`B4`) with 0% user disclosure (`SRR = 0%`) (Figure 1, p. 4; pp. 10–18).
Coding_Rationale: Studi lintas-platform produksi (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini) pada server MCP jarak jauh (Stream A) yang memperkenalkan metrik Self-Reporting Rate (`SRR`) di samping `ASR`.
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2; siap untuk rekonsiliasi dengan REVIEWER_1).
